Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- Failing test behavior and expectations:
  - testAvailableLocaleSet() calls LocaleUtils.availableLocaleSet() twice and expects:
    - a non-null Set,
    - the same instance returned both times (caching),
    - the Set to be unmodifiable,
    - the contents to match the JDK’s available locales.

- Relevant implementation:
  - Field:
    - org.apache.commons.lang.LocaleUtils.cAvailableLocaleSet
      - private static Set cAvailableLocaleSet;
      - Not initialized at declaration (defaults to null).
  - Lazy initialization:
    - org.apache.commons.lang.LocaleUtils.availableLocaleSet()
      - Initializes cAvailableLocaleSet on first call:
        - Creates new HashSet(availableLocaleList()), wraps it with Collections.unmodifiableSet, assigns to cAvailableLocaleSet, and returns it.
      - This satisfies the test’s identity and unmodifiable checks when invoked.
  - Problematic method:
    - org.apache.commons.lang.LocaleUtils.isAvailableLocale(Locale)
      - return cAvailableLocaleSet.contains(locale);
      - This method dereferences cAvailableLocaleSet directly without ensuring it has been initialized (i.e., without calling availableLocaleSet()).

- How the bug occurs:
  - Since cAvailableLocaleSet is null until availableLocaleSet() is called, any call to isAvailableLocale(Locale) before availableLocaleSet() will attempt to call contains on a null reference, causing a NullPointerException.
  - FindBugs correctly flagged this pattern: Field not initialized in constructor: org.apache.commons.lang.LocaleUtils.cAvailableLocaleSet, and isAvailableLocale(Locale) directly uses it.
  - While testAvailableLocaleSet itself drives availableLocaleSet() and would not trigger the NPE, the class contains an API (isAvailableLocale) that can NPE under normal usage if called first. This is the underlying defect described in the issue report.

- Summary:
  - Root cause: isAvailableLocale(Locale) bypasses the lazy initialization and dereferences cAvailableLocaleSet directly.
  - Symptom: NullPointerException when isAvailableLocale is invoked before availableLocaleSet.
  - The fix should ensure isAvailableLocale(Locale) uses the initialized set (e.g., by calling availableLocaleSet()) or initialize cAvailableLocaleSet eagerly.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
